answer: To enforce Sybil resistance across sensor agents deployed in a meadow, each node binds its identity to a recursive zero-knowledge commitment. If a malicious node attempts to forge the tracking data of a single sparrow, it must risk substantial staking collateral subject to automatic slashing penalties. Coupling this economic penalty with a cryptographic signal of unique elapsed time ensures that the expected utility of identity cloning is negative, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium.
